slides.title: A pre-cystectomy ctDNA quantitative threshold may identify patients who need additional NAT
slides.text:
A pre-cystectomy ctDNA quantitative threshold may identify patients who need additional NAT
Cohort
N = 59 evaluable patients at 3-month post-cystectomy landmark

Co-Primary Endpoint 1: Association
Pre-cystectomy ctDNA significantly predicts post-cystectomy MRD OR 1.89 per 10-fold increase (95% CI 1.37–2.76) p<0.001
Co-Primary Endpoint 2: Threshold Performance
Pre-cystectomy ctDNA cutoff (0.1 MTM/mL) Sensitivity ~82% | Specificity ~68% | PPV ~60% | NPV ~86% (bootstrap-validated)
Conclusion
Pre-cystectomy ctDNA above 0.1 MTM/mL reliably identifies patients at high risk for persistent MRD after surgery.

slides.title: Quantitative baseline ctDNA is prognostic prior to a new line of therapy
slides.text:
Quantitative baseline ctDNA is prognostic prior to a new line of therapy
Prior work: Qualitative baseline ctDNA associated with worse OS (HR 2.06)1
We retrospectively analyzed N=38 patients with metastatic bladder who had baseline ctDNA measured within 21 days prior to initiating a systemic therapy line (N=48 observations)
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-024-03091-7/figures/4

https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11175790/
21
Preliminary Data
Baseline Quantitative ctDNA and OS. Cox proportional hazards models evaluating baseline ctDNA (log10[ctDNA + 1]) and OS. HR >1 indicates increased risk of death.
